  (SELECT '1' AS id, 'b' AS a, date '2024-01-01' AS b) AS s
ON t.id = s.id

WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *;

-- Set tag `2024-01-01` -> [(1, b, 2024-01-01)]

VERSION AS OF '2024-01-01';

VERSION AS OF '2023-01-01'

VERSION AS OF '2024-01-01';

body:
Apache Iceberg version
1.4.3 (latest release)
Query engine
Spark
Please describe the bug 🐞
Reproduction:
Here's a simple unit test (can copy/paste this into TestMerge)
  @Test
  public void testMergeIntoNullValuesIssue() {
    createAndInitTable(
        "id INT, ts TIMESTAMP",
        "{ \"id\": 1, \"ts\": \"2000-01-01 00:00:00\" }\n" + "{ \"id\": 6, \"ts\": null }");

    createOrReplaceView(
        "source",
        "id INT NOT NULL, ts TIMESTAMP",
        "{ \"id\": 1, \"ts\": \"2000-01-01 00:00:00\" }\n");
    sql(
        "MERGE INTO %s t USING source s "
            + "ON t.id == s.id "
            + "WHEN MATCHED THEN "
            + "  UPDATE SET id=123, ts=current_timestamp()",
        commitTarget());

    sql("SELECT * FROM %s", commitTarget());
  }

In short:
1.) create a table
2.) insert some records where at least one of the records has a NULL column value.
3.) MERGE into the table with an update on matched records and set the column with the null value
Expected:
Record 1:  id=123, ts=current_timestamp()
Record 2: id=6, ts=null
However, in Spark 3.4 we get
Record 1:id=123, ts=current_timestamp()
Record 2: id=6, ts=01-01-1970 00:00:000 (basically Unix epoch. in practice it's timestamp with tz so it'll appear to your timezone)
I've done some debugging and what's happening is that the schema for the SparkWrite in 3.4 is treating all the fields as required, leading to the default behavior.
The reason why it's treating it as required is because the Spark expression nullability  is that the attributes for the fields https://github.com/apache/iceberg/blob/main/spark/v3.4/spark-extensions/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/sql/catalyst/analysis/RewriteMergeIntoTable.scala#L182 aren't being passed to the merge output schema during planning. This nullability needs to be passed correctly so that the null values in the non-matched cases get written correctly.
I'm currently looking into this, but creating this issue for tracking and awareness.
Important Note:
Spark 3.3 and Spark 3.5 do not have this bug based on my testing. MoR is unaffected.
title: Spark 3.4 MERGE INTO for CoW replacing NULL unmatched records with default values

Apache Iceberg version
1.4.3 (latest release)
Query engine
Spark
Please describe the bug 🐞
latestOffset call from SparkStreaming calculates maxFiles and maxRecords based on the snapshot after fromTs instead of the latest snapshot processed.
Because of this, records are never processed after first INT_MAX records starting from the snapshot after fromTs.  Iceberg falsely assumes that it has caught upto latest snapshot because output from latestOffset matches the last processed offset in checkpoint
startOffset that gets passed to this function is the initialOffset instead of latest offset stored in checkpoint and hence, the calculation of latestOffset is based on faulty input.
Confirmed this with SparkMicroBatchStreaming in AvailableNow mode in Spark 3.4. (maxFilesPerMicroBatch and maxRecordsPerMicroBatch were kept default)
To reproduce the bug -

Have more than INT_MAX records in the table
Use Sparkstreaming with AvailableNow and set fromTs to some timestamp. (INT_MAX records should exist after this timestamp). Let s1 be immediate snapshot after this fromTs
Start SparkStreaming. It will process everything from s1 to s2 where s2 is the latest snapshot before it spills over INT_MAX records
SparkStreaming saves the offset of s2 in <ckpt>/offsets/0
Rerun the SparkStreaming job with same parameters (same checkpoint location and same fromTs). Now, ideally, it should start processing from s2 untill some future snapshot s3 but the latestOffset buggy calculation returns the same snapshot s2 as the start point for it was s1
SparkStreaming job successfully terminates as the latest snapshot matches the last processed snapshot s2
title: `latestOffset` call in SparkMicroBatchStream limits files and records based on the startTs and not last processed snapshot
